rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a surface treatment to enhance oxide formation, while the target uses nanoindentation/friction simulation on an as-deposited coating without any surface treatment. These are different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies high-temperature wear testing up to 500°C under dry sliding with constant load, whereas the target uses nanoindentation/friction simulation at 300–1200 K (27–927°C) with a virtual indenter at 10 m/s. The temperature ranges overlap only partially, and the loading mode (sliding vs. indentation) differs.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes an oxide-based tribofilm as a sacrificial layer, while the target mechanism involves lattice disorder, dislocation density evolution, and stacking fault to disorder transition. These are different classes of mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved wear resistance with increasing temperature up to a threshold, whereas the target predicts stable wear resistance up to 600 K then a sharp decrease above 900 K. The direction of the predicted outcome is opposite.
